questions.explanation: Subtracting 1860 from 1885 gives twenty-five years of activity. A tempting mistake is to count inclusively and add one, but a span between two dates is their difference. The correct duration is therefore twenty-five years.

questions.topic: A fugue as a genre and as a technique
questions.stem: The chef's costing sheet calls a fugue a genre; what makes it a genre?

answer.exemplar: It is a genre because it is a complete, self-contained work with recognizable conventions and expected structure.

questions.explanation: A fugue is a genre when it stands as a complete work with conventions.

questions.topic: The interval an added voice takes above a chant melody
questions.stem: A costing sheet lists an added voice; which interval is most common in early organum?

options.text: A major third above the chant
An octave above the chant
A perfect fifth above the chant
A minor seventh above the chant

questions.explanation: Early organum favors an octave above; the other intervals belong to other practices.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The length of a cantus firmus measured in the voice above it
questions.stem: A recipe costing sheet gives 5 cantus firmus notes of 8 beats; what is total duration?
questions.explanation: Five cantus firmus notes of eight beats each total forty beats. A tempting error is to add the counts or treat beats as notes, which would give thirteen. Multiplying notes by beat length gives the duration, so forty is correct.
